The concern: "resume prefix validator compares prompt-id and response-index keys only while row_index carries answer_sha256 so regenerated-text cells resume stale vectors silently".

The validator now binds CONTENT as well as keys, in scripts/issue2658_capture.py:
- :86 answer_sha256 is a field on the row dataclass; :194 it is written into every row_index row.
- :353 the resume docstring states the row_index row "already carries answer_sha256 and each expected [row does too]" — i.e. the content hash is available to the comparison, which was the concern's premise.
- :373 the validator compares r["answer_sha256"] != c.answer_sha256 across the resumed prefix and :378 RAISES naming the count: "N resumed rows carry answer_sha256 differing from the [expected]". So a regenerated-text cell can no longer resume stale vectors silently — it fails loud.
- :565 states the contract explicitly: "KEYS and CONTENT (per-row answer_sha256) both bind".
- :468 additionally asserts gen-record integrity via C.assert_row_hash(r["text"], r["answer_sha256"]) before the row is consumed, and :577 refuses a shard existing beyond the contiguous resumed prefix.

Note the direction of the fix: it is fail-loud (raise), not silent re-derivation, which is the correct choice for a regenerated-text cell — the stale vectors must not be reused and must not be quietly recomputed under a resume that claims to have skipped work.

VERIFIED IMPLEMENTED by orchestrator code verification at round 12 — LEDGER CORRECTION, not a new fix. Raised round 1 (code-reviewer-lean-groupB).

The concern: "cell resume keys on raw_path alone while the gen manifest writes second so a crash between the two atomic writes strands the cell manifest-less forever".

scripts/issue2658_generate.py now carries a dedicated repair path, and its docstring names this exact failure:
- :591 resume_cell_with_manifest — :599 "raw-path-keyed resume would strand it manifest-less forever. manifest_rows_for_cell is a pure function of the resumed body, so the resume branch rewrites the manifest atomically".
- :604 loads the body via load_resume_cell (:573, "A completed cell resumes iff its stored fingerprint + count match" — fingerprint AND count, not raw_path presence alone).
- :607 write_jsonl_atomic(man_path, manifest_rows_for_cell(cell, body)) — the manifest is REWRITTEN atomically on every resume, so the crash-between-two-writes window self-heals on the next run instead of stranding the cell permanently.
- :701 the production loop calls resume_cell_with_manifest (not the bare load_resume_cell), so the repair is on the live path, not an unused helper.

The design point that closes it: because manifest_rows_for_cell is a PURE function of the resumed body, the rewrite needs no additional state and is idempotent — the manifest can always be reconstructed from the body that resumed, which is why "stranded forever" is no longer reachable.

Related: :296 the resume fingerprint is computed over GENERATING PARAMETERS per the #1336 machine-stability rule (never the raw bytes of a recomputed float array), so the resume key itself is machine-stable.

VERIFIED IMPLEMENTED by orchestrator code verification at round 12 — LEDGER CORRECTION, not a new fix. Raised round 1 (code-reviewer-lean-groupFIK).

The concern: "compose_packet and dispatch join items to the frozen key by row and item-id only so probe-confirmed post-freeze item drift ships silently under frozen tags mis-attaching human labels to the hidden [arm]".

scripts/issue2658_human_read.py now verifies CONTENT, not just the (row, item_id) join:
- :42 the module contract states it "verifies every item's display texts against the frozen content sha256s" — the join is content-bound.
- :396 _item_shas is documented as the "Single source for BOTH the frozen key's stored [shas] and the verification", so the freeze side and the check side cannot drift apart by construction (one function, two callers) — the failure mode a second, parallel hash implementation would reintroduce.
- :247-250 four sha fields participate: answer_sha256, evidence_sha256, raw_text_sha256, chat_template_sha256 — so drift in the answer text, the evidence packet, the raw text, or the chat template is all caught, not just the answer.
- :401 answer_sha256 is computed over it["answer_text"], i.e. over the DISPLAY text the reader actually sees, which is the right surface: a mismatch between what was frozen and what is shown is exactly what would mis-attach a human label.

This matters for the blinded-read integrity contract (.claude/rules/blinded-reads.md): the blinding key must be frozen BEFORE the first packet is sent and must not be reconstructable post-hoc to fit the answer. Verifying display text against the frozen shas is what makes the frozen tags trustworthy; without it, post-freeze drift would silently re-map labels to the wrong hidden arm.

Related surfaces confirmed present: :100 ORDER_DOMAIN is a sha-derived deterministic order, :102 per-reader shuffle is seeded from sha256('i2658-reader-order|'+reader+'|'+key_fingerprint) — so the reader-order domain is also keyed to the frozen key's fingerprint. (The open CONCERN identical-reader-packet-order and NIT reader-order-distinctness-statistical track refinements of that ordering, separately from this sha-verification concern.)
